raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Overview `BasevLLMParameter` overrides `__torch_function__` with a Python classmethod. The override only forwards to `Parameter`'s disabled implementation. Since #62326, quantized weights and scales stay `BasevLLMParameter` subclasses after `process_weights_after_loading`. As a result, every eager op that takes one of them goes through Python `handle_torch_function`. This PR removes the override. The subclasses then inherit `torch._C._disabled_torch_function_impl` from `Parameter`, which torch short-circuits in C++. ## Claims - Fixes a host-side regression from #62326 on steps that run outside full CUDA graphs: prefill and mixed prefill+decode steps. - GLM-5.2-FP8, TP4 on one GB300 node, same-node A/B against main on 3 nodes: - c1 TTFT for 1024-token prompts drops from 220.4 to 207.0 ms (-6.1%); - worker `execute_model` host time drops 8.7 ms per prefill step (-4.5%) and 11.2 ms per mixed step (-4.4%); - TPOT is unchanged: pure decode replays full CUDA graphs and dispatches no ops. - No behavior change: - #62326's guarantees are untouched: the same parameter objects, classes, loader attributes and `data_ptr`; - op results were plain tensors before (`super().__torch_function__` is the disabled implementation) and still are; - greedy outputs are identical and GSM8K is within run-to-run noise. ## Validation ### Serving: GLM-5.2-FP8 (`zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`) Setup: - TP4, one GB300 node, MRV2, default torch.compile and CUDA graphs; - `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl`; - `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`; - `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos`. At c8/c32, new prompts arrive while others decode, so those runs mix prefill and decode steps. Method: - Each Slurm job runs on one node. It first starts a throwaway server: the first server on a node is 10-15 ms slower at c1 TTFT, so it is excluded. - It then interleaves `main`, `this PR` and two other variants not covered here, twice each. - Values are the mean of each variant's 2 runs on that node; the delta is against `main` on the same node. Median TTFT (ms): | node / job | workload | main | this PR | delta | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | c1, 24 prompts | 223.5 | **204.7** | **-18.7** | | 2 | c1 | 220.5 | **210.5** | **-10.1** | | 3 | c1 | 217.3 | **205.7** | **-11.6** | | **mean** | **c1** | **220.4** | **207.0** | **-13.5 (-6.1%)** | | mean | c8, 160 prompts | 465.7 | **453.1** | **-12.6** | | mean | c32, 320 prompts | 810.2 | **762.1** | **-48 (noisy)** | Median TPOT (ms): c1 9.70 vs 9.69, c8 14.30 vs 14.27, c32 25.80 vs 25.77. Host time of the worker's `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`: a `perf_counter` wrapper, with steps split by kind. Values are the p50 per rank, averaged over the 4 ranks, from the same runs (c1 + c8 workloads): | node / job | prefill-only step: main | this PR | delta | mixed step: main | this PR | delta | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 189.8 | **181.0** | **-8.8** | 254.5 | **239.3** | **-15.2** | | 2 | 192.5 | **184.2** | **-8.3** | 257.4 | **248.6** | **-8.8** | | 3 | 191.7 | **182.8** | **-8.9** | 254.0 | **244.5** | **-9.6** | An earlier stack-sampling profile of the prefill step put about 14% of its host time in `parameter.py:__torch_function__`. It was called from the FP8 linear apply, the DeepGEMM / per-token-group quant wrappers and the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 MoE calls. Dense BF16 model (Qwen3-0.6B, TP1): no measurable change (c1 TTFT 22.4 vs 22.3/23.3 ms, c32 within noise). Its unquantized weights were already `ModelWeightParameter` before #62326, and its steps are less host-bound. ### Correctness - Greedy, `temperature=0`, 34 fixed prompts with 128 tokens each at c1: outputs are byte-identical to `main` in 3/3 runs on 3 nodes. - GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64): | | runs | accuracy | |---|---|---| | main | 5 | 95.0, 94.2, 94.2, 94.9, 94.8 | | this PR | 3 | 94.5, 94.1, 94.2 | The kernels and their inputs are unchanged, so the spread is batch-composition noise at concurrency 64. Main alone spans 94.2 to 95.0. - The serving runs use torch.compile (Dynamo traces modules with these parameters) and CUDA graphs. They start and produce identical outputs without the override. ### Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \ tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "not test_reload_weights" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \ -k "test_reload_weights and (FP8_BLOCK or FP8_DYNAMIC)" pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/parameter.py tests/model_executor/test_utils.py ``` Results on GB300 (this PR vs `main`, same commands): | test | this PR | main | |---|---|---| | `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` | 14 passed (incl. the new test) | 13 passed | | `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` | 10 passed | 10 passed | | `test_reload.py -k "not test_reload_weights"` | 70 passed, 2 xpassed, 2 failed | same 2 failures | | `test_reload_weights` FP8_BLOCK / FP8_DYNAMIC (TP1, TP2) | 4 passed, 4 skipped | 4 passed, 4 skipped | | `pre-commit` | all hooks pass | | Both `test_reload.py` failures also fail on `main` and are unrelated: - `test_kv_scale_reload`: perplexity 6575.09 after reload, identical on `main`. - `test_online_quantize_reload[...Qwen3-0.6B...fp8_per_tensor-1]`: when it runs after that failure in the same session, the forked engine core hits `CUDA error: initialization error`. This also happens on `main`. The test passes when run alone on both trees. New test `test_kept_param_ops_skip_python_torch_function`: - it checks that a param kept by `replace_parameter` keeps its class; - that `torch.overrides.has_torch_function` is false for it, so eager ops dispatch in C++; - and that op results are still plain tensors. ## Details **Root cause.** - #23036 added the override, together with a torch-2.7-only `traceable_tensor_subclasses` Dynamo workaround (`_torch27_patch_tensor_subclasses`). - #33209 removed the workaround when torch < 2.8 support was dropped, but left the override. - The override does nothing at runtime: it calls `super().__torch_function__`, i.e. `Parameter`'s `_disabled_torch_function_impl`. Its presence still makes torch treat these parameters as having a Python torch function. Every op, and every Python-level `Tensor` method or property access on them, then goes through `handle_torch_function` and the classmethod. - Before #62326, most quantization methods re-registered plain `Parameter`s in `process_weights_after_loading`, so FP8/FP4 weights and scales did not pay this cost. - #62326 keeps the original objects so that reload and RL refit keep their loader metadata. The quantized weights and scales of every linear and MoE layer now pay this cost on every eager op. **Fix.** Delete the override. `BasevLLMParameter` then behaves like `torch.nn.Parameter`: - `__torch_function__` is the disabled implementation; - `isinstance`, class, attributes and object identity are unchanged; - op results stay plain tensors. This keeps everything #62326 relies on. A global monkey-patch or unwrapping params after loading would undo #62326's goal. **Scope.** - Only steps that dispatch ops eagerly benefit: prefill, mixed and piecewise steps. Full-CUDA-graph decode is unchanged. - The gain grows with the number of quantized layers and ops per step. ## Why this is not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open` searches found no PR that touches `BasevLLMParameter.__torch_function__` or the overhead from #62326. Search terms: `__torch_function__`, `BasevLLMParameter`, `replace_parameter`, `62326`, `torch_function overhead`, `handle_torch_function`, `ModelWeightParameter overhead`. - #62407 (part 3 of the #62326 series, open) changes which params stay registered and does not touch `parameter.py`. This PR is independent of it and helps it as well. - The only earlier change to the override is #25613, reverted by #25681. It returned `NotImplemented` on torch < 2.8 for a Dynamo bug and did not remove the dispatch. - No upstream issue covers it. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, write the change and its test, and run the benchmarks and evals above. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the measurements. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

files.patch:
@@ -268,6 +268,34 @@ def weight_loader(param: torch.Tensor, loaded_weight: torch.Tensor) -> None:
     assert torch.equal(layer.weight, torch.ones(4, 4))
 
 
+def test_kept_param_ops_skip_python_torch_function(single_rank_tp: None) -> None:
+    """Kept vLLM params must dispatch eager ops like a plain Parameter: a Python
+    `__torch_function__` would put every op on them through the interpreter."""
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.register_parameter(
+        "weight",
+        ModelWeightParameter(
+            data=torch.zeros(4, 4),
+            input_dim=1,
+            output_dim=0,
+            weight_loader=lambda param, loaded_weight: None,
+        ),
+    )
+    replace_parameter(layer, "weight", torch.ones(4, 4))
+
+    assert type(layer.weight) is ModelWeightParameter
+    # A kept param must dispatch like a plain Parameter. Compare against a
+    # plain Parameter rather than asserting an absolute False: on ROCm,
+    # has_torch_function can return True for plain Parameters too.
+    plain = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(4, 4))
+    assert torch.overrides.has_torch_function(
+        (layer.weight,)
+    ) == torch.overrides.has_torch_function((plain,))
+    out = layer.weight + 1
+    assert type(out) is torch.Tensor
+    assert torch.equal(out, torch.full((4, 4), 2.0))
+
+

     that transposes it must not leave the post-transform dims on it."""
